what: what a public republication of the pretraining corpus would carry, and what still gates it
scope: Salesforce/GiftEvalPretrain only. GIFT-Eval itself is the evaluation data and is never republished.

held_out_description_files.question: does any source ship files that describe the held-out set, the way pdearena ships pde_test_seed_*.yaml?
held_out_description_files.method: enumerated every path in sources.lock.json and matched test/seed/config/split/eval as path tokens
held_out_description_files.conclusion: none. The corpus and the evaluation data are separate repositories, so a corpus release carries no test data at all and needs no truncation. This is structurally simpler than pde-surrogate, where the held-out trajectories live inside the training files.

what_a_release_must_exclude.why: these were measured to contain GIFT-Eval evaluation series up to an affine transform (m4_hourly is pedestrian_counts + 10, r = 1.000000 across the whole series including its test horizon; docs/validation/corpus_leakage_verified.json). Upstream advertises the corpus as non-leaking and ships them anyway. Republishing them under our name would propagate that leak, so a release must carry the 81-directory allow-list rather than all 152.

licence_position.why: LargeST is 17.81 GB and 43.1% of the allow-list and is CC BY-NC 4.0. CC BY-NC permits redistribution with attribution and the notice carried through, so a release is possible, but it cannot be labelled Apache-2.0 as the upstream card is. Salesforce took the same position one layer up: every Moirai checkpoint trained on this corpus ships cc-by-nc-4.0.

resolved_clear.finding: these reached the corpus through the Monash Time Series Forecasting Archive, which is CC-BY-4.0. Its 'intended for research purpose' note is a request rather than a licence term and does not restrict redistribution.

unresolved.finding: sourced from Kaggle competitions directly rather than through Monash. Their rules pages require a login, so the redistribution clause could not be read. UPSTREAM_LICENSES.md records 'several forbid redistribution' from a survey that was not individually re-read, and that remains the state of knowledge.
options: read the four competition rule pages from a logged-in session
drop the four directories, which costs 1.94% of the allow-list

conclusion: A corpus release is technically straightforward - no truncation, no held-out description files, 81 of 152 directories. Two decisions gate it: label the release CC BY-NC 4.0, and either clear or drop the four Kaggle-sourced directories worth 1.94%.
